topic: Tuskegee Airmen's 'never lost a bomber' myth vs. the real WWII record (27 lost)
title: The Tuskegee Airmen 'Never Lost A Bomber' Myth, Debunked
description: AI-narrated commentary on the real WWII combat record behind the Tuskegee Airmen's famous 'never lost a bomber' reputation, and the 1945 magazine claim that started the myth.

hook_candidates.text: This WWII group supposedly never lost a bomber.
This WWII fighter group actually lost 27 bombers it was escorting.
What if the most repeated fact about a legendary WWII fighter group was false?
A single 1945 magazine article about Black fighter pilots got repeated as fact for 60 years.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the uncle who repeats the Tuskegee Airmen's perfect record like it's gospel, because they want to show him the real number.
contradicted_belief: Most people still believe the WWII myth that the Tuskegee Airmen never lost a single escorted bomber.
closing_comment: The real number, 27 lost bombers, doesn't erase how good the Tuskegee Airmen actually were, it just makes the truth more impressive than the myth.

sources.note: Confirms the 99th Fighter Squadron's first combat mission flew June 2, 1943, from Tunisia, North Africa.
Confirms Air Force historical research found 27 bombers the 332nd Fighter Group escorted were shot down, debunking the 'never lost a bomber' myth.
